jobs.prompt: Fix the second review round of the process-control part (tools/server-restart.mjs, tools/update-pending.mjs, tools/watch-cli.mjs, tools/watch-server.mjs, tools/swarm/core-52.mjs). Finding 1 is HIGH and must be fixed first and tested end to end with a fake board that starts on a random port: the restart must find the new port from the rewritten board record and confirm the new version there, and must never SIGTERM a healthy new replacement. Also fix 2 (Ctrl-C/SIGTERM during --when-idle: after cleanup remove handlers and exit 130/143), 3 (exact token comparison, require runner path, fail closed when start time unknown), 4 (delete the record only on a positive mismatch, never on a failed ps), 5 (EPERM means alive but not ours: keep the record, report), 6 (cross-process file lock for the pending file and the held log; no recreation after cleanup), 7 (a real parentOf using ps -o ppid= with a bounded walk, passed by the caller), 8 (verify the wiring of waitBeforeLaunchingWork and runWhenIdleUpdate in tools/swarm.mjs and the tools/swarm modules covers every work-launching command and no read-only command; fix gaps), 9 (a restart lock so two concurrent updates never both signal), 10 (filter env through the safe subset on read), 11 (manualCommand quotes the node path), 12 (trim the held log). The reviewer text follows as data: Findings 1. High, tools/watch-cli.mjs tools/server-restart.mjs. The board restart does not reuse the port. - The board starts with port: 0 (watch-server.mjs), so it gets a random port. Its recorded argv is ['watch','--all'] with no port flag. - The restarted board therefore listens on a new port. pollNewVersion polls the old record.port, never sees the new version, and treats the attempt as failed. - It then SIGTERMs the healthy new board and retries once, which also fails. The user ends up with no board and a "replacement did not come up" report. - The intent was "same port", and this breaks the board case. - Fix: after spawn, find the new port from the rewritten board record, as pollRemoteFile does for remote, and confirm through that. 2. Medium, tools/update-pending.mjs. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM during --when-idle does not stop the update. - abortHandler adds listeners for SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP, which suppresses Node's default exit. It only removes the pending record, and exits only if onAbort does. - The wait loop keeps polling without the hold and can still run performUpdate. - Fix: after cleanup, remove the handlers and re-raise or exit (130 or 143). 3. Medium, tools/server-restart.mjs :124-138. The identity check is a loose substring match. - Any process whose command contains swarm.mjs, watch and --all passes for a board. Argv tokens of 2 characters or fewer are skipped. - If ps etimes is unparsable, the start-time check is skipped entirely. - A reused pid belonging to another swarm process can pass. This is narrow, but it is the safety property the task asked about. - Fix: compare tokens exactly, require the runner path, and fail closed when the start time is unknown. 4. Medium, tools/server-restart.mjs. A transient ps failure ("could not read process command line") deletes the record of a live server. That server is never restarted and the next update cannot find it. Only delete the record on a positive mismatch. 5. Medium, tools/server-restart.mjs. pidAlive treats EPERM as dead, so the record is removed for a pid that exists but is not ours. This is harmless by intent, but the record is silently deleted. 6. Medium, tools/update-pending.mjs :156-178. Concurrent launchers and the updater race on the pending file. - withHeldLock only serialises within one process. Across processes, rewritePending is a read-modify-write, so heldPids entries can be lost. - A late rewrite can also recreate the record after the updater's cleanup removed it. While the updater is alive this holds new launches until expiry. - Fix: use a file lock (the unused HELD_LOCK_BASENAME suggests this was intended), or derive held pids from the append-only log. 7. Medium, tools/update-pending.mjs. defaultParentOf always returns null, so ancestor matching does nothing unless a caller passes parentOf. In core-52.mjs I found no such caller. A subprocess of a held autopilot or go loop is then counted as busy work, which can make the updater wait until timeout and exit 75. A held launcher is only recognised by its own pid. 8. Medium, tools/swarm/core-52.mjs, tools/update-pending.mjs. I found no call to waitBeforeLaunchingWork or runWhenIdleUpdate in core-52.mjs. - The wiring for the hold and --when-idle must be in swarm.mjs or another file I couldn't open, so I could not check bypass or leakage into read-only commands. - I also could not check whether a crashed update can strand the machine. Within this module the stale rules look sound: the updater refreshes the expiry on every poll, and the record is ignored once its pid is dead or it has expired. 9. Medium, tools/server-restart.mjs. Nothing serialises two concurrent swarm update runs. - Both can SIGTERM the same pid and both can spawn a replacement. - The second spawn then fails on the port, and the failure path kills "its" new pid. - Fix: take a restart lock, for example by reusing the pending slot. 10. Low, tools/server-restart.mjs. record.env and record.cwd are not validated. - Env is only type-checked as an object, and a forged record could set keys like NODE_OPTIONS. - The spawn is argv-array only (no shell) and cwd is checked to be a directory, so this is adversarial only. - Fix: filter env through safeEnvSubset on read. 11. Low, tools/server-restart.mjs. manualCommand exports env names without values (export KEY), so the printed command does not reproduce the environment. process.execPath is also unquoted. 12. Low, tools/update-pending.mjs. .update-pending-held.log is append-only and never cleaned. 13. Low, tools/watch-server.mjs. /api/health is correct: it returns 421 for remote servers and for non-loopback Host values. It needs no token and returns {ok, version, pid}, which is minor information for local processes. 14. Low, tools/update-pending.mjs. The 75 exit is set via process.exitCode on timeout, which is fine. The caller must not override it. I could not check that. 15. Adversarial-only, low. A forged record with matching swarm.mjs, watch and --all text in an unrelated process's command line could get that process SIGTERMed. A forged pending record could hold launches until expiry. On the process-control points that weren't findings: restart never uses SIGKILL, the port-free wait is bounded at 15s, the SIGTERM wait at 15s and each health poll at 20s. Terminal-mode servers are left running with a message. --when-idle is bounded by timeoutMinutes.  New tests in tests/server-restart-round2.test.mjs and tests/update-pending-round2.test.mjs. Fix every finding that is real (verify each against the code first; a finding that is already handled gets a one-line note in the test file header instead). Keep every existing test passing. Add a test per fixed finding in a new test file named in the task. Do not edit tools/swarm.mjs unless a call must pass a new option. Never import install.mjs statically from new modules. Hermetic tests, no ambient environment, no network, no token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: only the named files and their tests change.

Fix the second review round of the registry, scratch and hook part (tools/projects.mjs, tools/scratch-roots.mjs, tools/handbuild.mjs, tools/handbuild-commands.mjs, tools/board-inbox.mjs, tools/githook-check.mjs, tools/git-hooks.mjs, tools/watch-cli.mjs, tools/inbox.mjs, tools/phone.mjs). Priorities: the unmounted mountpoint case (only prune when the parent directory is a different device than the grandparent check does not apply: simplest safe rule: never prune an entry whose path is under /Volumes, /mnt or /media or whose parent is empty or a mount point, and report it unreachable instead), forget --scratch must use the strict rule, a wrong SWARM_SCRATCH_BASE must never turn real projects into scratch (the base must also not contain a registered project that has its own .git folder outside the scratch convention: refuse such a base with a warning), the commit-msg hook must not refuse commits when node is present but the check crashes (any non-violation failure exits 0 with a warning; only an explicit violation exit code, for example 3, blocks), the Manifest subject rule only for Manifest: Manifests: or Manifest for, phone counts exclude scratch, symlinked user hooks are backed up before replacement, chained hooks that are not executable are run through sh, remove dead branches in shouldSkipCommitMsgCheck (git passes only the message file, detect amend or merge from git state: MERGE_HEAD, rebase-merge and the commit message source argument that git passes as the second hook argument for commit-msg is not given, so use .git state only), the right git config key (core.commentChar, with auto handling), a hooks path shared by several repos (core.hooksPath) is reported and the hook is written only when it is inside this repo or the owner passes --force-shared, registeredScratchHandbuildRoot also covers a path whose real path is inside the scratch base even when unregistered, remove stack-trace sniffing in tools/board-inbox.mjs completely (explicit forOwner option from watch-cli, the phone and inbox callers: the board path must pass it), and the install-root refusal fails closed (when the install root cannot be resolved, refuse forget of any path that contains a tools/swarm.mjs file). The reviewer text follows as data: ## Status of the earlier HIGH findings 1. Reused pid signalled: I can't verify this one. The signalling code isn't in any file I was given, and I didn't read the tests. It stays open for another reviewer. 2. Registry rows dropped on stat errors: Mostly fixed. Only ENOENT or ENOTDIR with a readable parent counts as "missing", and every other error or timeout keeps the row. One gap remains, in finding 1 below. 3. Broad test-folder rule applied to inbox and auto-deny: Fixed for the inbox and the auto-deny. Both use the strict rule. forget --scratch still uses the broad rule (finding 2), and a wrong SWARM_SCRATCH_BASE can still swallow real projects (finding 3). 4. Commit hook locking out commits: Partly fixed. A missing node or missing script now skips the check. A node that is present but crashes still blocks every commit (finding 4). ## Findings 1. Medium: unmounted drive or share drops real projects (tools/projects.mjs :118-148, :333). - The rule is "missing" when the folder gives ENOENT and its parent is readable. - On Linux an unmounted /mnt/share leaves an empty mountpoint, so /mnt/share/proj gives ENOENT with a readable parent. On macOS this happens when the mount point itself is the project (/Volumes/X). - Every owner-path listProjects call then silently rewrites the registry without those rows. forget --missing has the same hole. - The rows come back the next time swarm runs in the folder, but addedAt and the name are lost, and the project vanishes from the inbox until then. - Fix: don't prune on the first sighting. Record missingSince and prune only after a grace period such as 7 days. Alternatively hide missing rows without deleting them, and leave deletion to explicit forget. 2. Medium: forget --scratch uses the broad rule (tools/projects.mjs). - It ORs in isTestTempRoot, which contradicts the header in scratch-roots.mjs where forget is listed as strict. - A real project at ~/work/tests/app or ~/test/app is forgotten. - --yes is only needed above 3 entries, so a single such match is removed with no prompt. - Fix: use strict only. 3. Medium: a wrong SWARM_SCRATCH_BASE can turn real projects into scratch (tools/scratch-roots.mjs :82). - scratchRootList is called without registeredRoots, so the "inside a registered project" guard never runs from isScratchRoot. - Only root, home and ancestors of home are rejected. Setting the variable to ~/code or /opt is accepted. - Every project under it is then hidden from the inbox and phone, and its handbuild requests are auto-denied. - resolveScratchBase also calls console.warn on every isScratchRoot call when the value is invalid. That means one warning per project per listing. - Fix: require the base to contain no registered roots, or to be named like scratch or sit under the temp dir. Warn once. 4. Medium: commit-msg hook refuses every commit when node is present but crashes (tools/git-hooks.mjs tools/githook-check.mjs). - The shell wrapper treats exit code 1 as "refuse". Node also exits 1 for an import or syntax error. That happens when the install dir is half-updated, a sibling module is missing, or the node version is too old. - In that case all commits are blocked. - Fix: have the checker refuse with a distinct code, for example 65, and have the wrapper treat everything else as infrastructure. 5. Medium: broad Manifest subject rule (tools/githook-check.mjs). - Any subject starting with "Manifest " is a manifest commit, except "Manifest parser:". - A commit like "Manifest v3 migration" with src/ files staged is refused. - There is no bypass: the guardOff and agent-session gates are not applied to commit-msg. - Fix: require manifest:, manifests: or manifest for, or add an env bypass. 6. Medium: Needs-you phone counts don't exclude scratch (tools/board-inbox.mjs). - scratchRoots is built from ownerProjects, which has already had scratch removed. The set is therefore always empty, except in the test fallback. - Scratch phone issues are counted in open and confirming. - phoneIssue also requires rec.root, while open doesn't. If records lack root, confirming goes negative or zero. I didn't confirm what fields the phone records carry. - Fix: call isScratchRoot(rec.root, {strict:true}) on each asked record, using the root from the record or the key. 7. Medium: the broad rule hides real projects from the board (tools/scratch-roots.mjs tools/projects.mjs). - The home exemption only covers segments that are part of the home path itself. - ~/dev/test/app, ~/Documents/tests/x, ~/work/temp/foo, or a project whose folder is named test is hidden from the default board list. - Fix: exempt anything under home or the install root, not just segments of the home path itself. Alternatively apply the broad rule only under the OS temp dir. 8. Medium: install deletes a symlinked user hook without backing it up (tools/git-hooks.mjs). - unlinkSync is called on a symlinked hook, so the user's shared or symlinked commit-msg is dropped. Uninstall can't restore it. - Fix: rename the symlink to .before-swarm instead. 9. Low–medium: the chained user hook fails if it isn't executable (tools/git-hooks.mjs :49, :75). - The wrapper runs $PREV whenever it is a file. Git itself ignores a non-executable hook. - A backed-up non-exec hook gives exit 126, which refuses the commit. - Fix: add -x "$PREV" to the test. - sort -V may not exist on every platform, in which case PREV ends up empty. Uninstall sorts lexicographically, so -10 sorts before -2. 10. Low–medium: shouldSkipCommitMsgCheck has dead code (tools/githook-check.mjs). - Git passes a hook only the message file. process.argv never has --amend, and git doesn't set GIT_COMMIT_MSG, so those branches never fire. - GITMERGE_AUTOEDIT is a real variable. .git/MERGE_HEAD is wrong in linked worktrees, where .git is a file. - Merge, fixup and squash subjects don't match the manifest regex anyway, so there is no live bug today. The code gives false confidence. 11. Low–medium: wrong git config key (tools/githook-check.mjs). - It reads commit.commentChar. The real key is core.commentChar, so a custom comment character is ignored. - The first line of a comment-leading message is then misparsed, which can mis-classify the subject. 12. Low–medium: hooks path may be shared (tools/git-hooks.mjs). - With core.hooksPath set to a shared directory such as husky or a global one, the hook is installed there and applies to other, non-swarm repos. This includes the manifest rule from finding 5. - Fix: refuse or warn when the hooks path is outside the repo. 13. Low–medium: registeredScratchHandbuildRoot only auto-denies registered scratch roots (tools/handbuild-commands.mjs :52). - A scratch project that was forgotten or never registered gets a normal request. The output says "waiting for the owner", which is false because the inbox hides it. - Fix: auto-deny on the strict rule alone. 14. Low: stack-trace sniffing in production code (tools/board-inbox.mjs). - With ownerInbox undefined and every project scratch, boardInbox returns all projects when the stack mentions board-inbox.test.mjs or watch-cli.mjs. - That means the real board path shows scratch projects if watch-cli doesn't pass ownerInbox. - Fix: remove the sniffing and make callers pass ownerInbox explicitly. 15. Low: - Install-root refusal fails open (tools/projects.mjs). If stableInstallDir can't be resolved, install is null and nothing is refused. - Misleading dry-run (tools/projects.mjs). A non-"damaged" read error such as EACCES prints "nothing to forget" with exit 0. - Redundant branch (tools/projects.mjs). Both arms are the same, and wrote is unused. - Stale-lock race (tools/projects.mjs). Two waiters can both judge the lock stale. The second rm can then delete the first waiter's fresh lock. A holder that runs longer than 30 seconds also loses its lock. Adversarial-only (low): - A committed .swarm-scratch file or .project-swarm.json with scratch:true hides a project, because strict doesn't exempt the install root or home subtrees. - Directory symlink tricks at the registry path are handled by resolveRegistryTarget. Forget itself looks safe: it writes only the registry file, atomically through a tmp file and rename under the lock. An unmatched path aborts the whole forget before any write, and an exact path or id match is required. FAIL New tests in tests/registry-round2.test.mjs and tests/commit-msg-round2.test.mjs. Fix every finding that is real (verify each against the code first; a finding that is already handled gets a one-line note in the test file header instead). Keep every existing test passing. Add a test per fixed finding in a new test file named in the task. Do not edit tools/swarm.mjs unless a call must pass a new option. Never import install.mjs statically from new modules. Hermetic tests, no ambient environment, no network, no token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: only the named files and their tests change.
